title: Still Waters
subtitle: Four weeks of prayer and breath, learning to be still enough to hear God.

week_list.title: Settling the Body
week_list.opening_line: Your attention is not yours right now, and you can have it back in ninety seconds with nothing but your own breath.
week_list.stakes: Skip this week and everything after it fails. You'll be doing a body practice with your mind, which is like opening a door by thinking about the handle.
week_list.pull_quote: You cannot give away something you are not holding.

blocks.v: Nobody built you a room, and nobody gave you a progression. Both are fixable in four weeks, and neither is a fact about your character. This week is the progression: the body that can hold silence, before you ask it to sit in silence.

blocks.title: The four shapes — the whole program

items.head: The long exhale
items.sub: Out longer than in. Four in, six out. Nasal, unforced, no holding.

items.head: The anchor
items.sub: One point of contact, chosen before you sit. Both feet on the floor, or the ribs, or one word. One.

items.head: The return
items.sub: You notice you left. You come back on the next exhale. No commentary and no apology.

items.head: The open hand
items.sub: Palms up on your thighs for three breaths before you stand.

blocks.title: How stillness is usually taught, and how it is trained

left.head: The way you were taught
items: Day one is ten minutes of silence
No prerequisite, no progression, no shapes
You are graded on how peaceful it felt
When it fails, the diagnosis is your discipline

right.head: The way a gymnast is trained
items: Day one is one shape, drilled, for two minutes
Nothing is attempted until what is under it is automatic
You are graded on whether you came back
When it fails, the question is which prerequisite went soft

blocks.v: Body first, because the body is the door. Attention second, because attention is the offering. Him third, because He is the point. Three words: settle, gather, give.

week_list.title: Giving It Away On Purpose
week_list.opening_line: A settled body with nowhere to point is a nap. This week you give your attention to Him, by name, out loud.
week_list.stakes: Skip this week and you finish the program calmer and exactly as alone as it found you, which you can get free on your phone.
week_list.pull_quote: The wandering is not the failure. The returning is the practice, and every wander hands you another rep.

blocks.v: Prayer is address. Somebody is there. The wandering mind is not the enemy in this room — the commentary you run about it is.

items.head: His name for it
items.sub: Shepherd. Father. Provider. Rock. The One who sees. Whatever is honest.

items.head: Build it
items.sub: Half on the inhale, usually who He is. Half on the exhale, usually what you are doing or asking. Under nine words total.

items.sub: In the kitchen. Not in your head. If it is clunky in the mouth it will be abandoned by Thursday.

week_list.title: What Comes Up, and How to Stay
week_list.opening_line: Silence is not peace. Silence is an amplifier, and around day twelve you find out what it has been covering.
week_list.stakes: Skip this week and you get four calm weeks and the same locked door. Stay in it and something you have been carrying gets set down.
week_list.pull_quote: You are not staying with it alone, and the move is not I can handle this. The move is I don't have to leave, because I'm not the one holding it.

blocks.v: Staying is not grit. It is a trained skill, built entirely on the return — because the return is the way back, and without it, staying with what comes up is just going under and calling it depth.

blocks.title: The five steps — the way back, in a chair

items.head: Notice you want to leave
items.sub: The dread, the weight, the wave of get-out-of-this-chair. Name that it has arrived.

items.head: Name it in three words, out loud
items.sub: Grief. The list. Restlessness. The thing. Whatever it is, plainly.

items.head: Feet and hands
items.sub: Feet flat, hands open. Four long exhales.

items.head: Say it to Him plainly
items.sub: I have been carrying this. You are not carrying it alone.

items.head: Ninety more seconds, then stop
items.sub: Stopping on purpose is as much of the skill as staying.

blocks.v: Silence surfaces things — that is not a side effect, it is the mechanism, and it is why this works. Some of what comes up in a quiet room is not a cut corner and must never be treated like one. Grief is not a gap in your training. Old material arriving with your whole body attached to it is not a gap in your training. Panic is not a gap in your training. That belongs in a licensed room with a person trained for it, and needing that is normal — it is not a failure of the practice and it is not a failure of you. A cut corner is boring and it responds; you close it and the thing eases within a few days. The other kind arrives at full size, has its own history, and after a week of doing everything right it is exactly the same size.

week_list.title: Building Your Own Room
week_list.principle: falling is routine — the repair is written in advance
week_list.opening_line: You have had a room built for you for three weeks. This week you find out how it was made, and you build one that stands up when nobody is holding the clock but you.
week_list.stakes: Skip this and you bought four nice weeks — and eleven weeks from now you will file that away as more evidence in the case you are building against yourself. Do it and you own a practice for the rest of your life.
week_list.pull_quote: Everyone can keep a floor for eleven days. The women still praying next spring are the ones who had a plan for the Wednesday they didn't.

blocks.v: The room was never mine. Somebody else decides when it starts and stops, holds the clock, is responsible for what comes next — so the part of you that is permanently on duty gets to stand down. This week you build that room for yourself.

items.head: Write the heading first
items.sub: This has to survive my worst week. Look at it the whole time you write the rest.

items.head: The daily floor
items.sub: What, how long, where, and a clock time. Could you do it on the worst day of last year? If no, halve it. If still no, halve it again.

items.head: The four-minute version
items.sub: Written separately, one sentence. Yours will be close to: extended exhales, the phrase, one line to Him.

items.head: The weekly beam
items.sub: One longer practice, with a named day and a named hour. No hour named means you have a wish, not a beam.

items.head: The repair
items.sub: One sentence, written before you need it, ending: and I say nothing to anyone about the gap.

items.head: The witness
items.sub: One woman by name, and the group feed. Both, not either.

items.head: The card
items.sub: Copy the floor, the four-minute version, the beam and the repair onto one card. Nothing else fits.

blocks.v: Four Minutes

God took everything. That's not a figure of speech — material things left my hands, until there wasn't much left to hold onto. I had built a life around what I owned and what I could point to, and I hadn't noticed how much ego was propping up the whole structure until the structure was gone. I'd known God since I was a kid. Never doubted Him, always called myself a Christian. But knowing Him and being humbled by Him turned out to be two different rooms, and I had never actually been in the second one.

There was nothing productive to do about it. No workout that fixes it. No goal to set and hit. I could not earn my way out and I could not perform my way past it, and performing was the only language I had ever really spoken. All that was left underneath it was the pain itself, with no project to turn it into.

I did not handle it well. I did not sit with it because I had learned how to be still — I sat with it because I had run out of other options, and I was bad at it the whole way through. It was never discipline. Two things were missing, both structural, both fixable in four weeks, and neither of them anything to do with your character. Nobody built you a room. And nobody gave you a progression. The next four weeks are those two things.
The four shapes
Four shapes. Four weeks. Nothing gets added, and when something goes wrong in week three we go back and find out which of the four went soft.

blocks.cue: Eight stops, feet upward. One question at each — what is true here. Nothing is a real answer.

items.head: Eight stops, feet upward
items.sub: Feet, calves and knees, thighs and hips, belly, chest, hands and arms, shoulders and throat, jaw and face.

items.head: One question at every stop
items.sub: What is true here.

items.head: Nothing is a real answer
items.sub: No relaxing instruction, no letting anything soften. This is inventory, not repair.

items.head: One full breath through the whole body
items.sub: Then — this is where my life is happening, and I have not been home in a while.

blocks.v: The list that arrives in a quiet room is a bodyguard, and it shows up when something quieter is about to get through. It is not a to-do list. Write it down, three words per item, and go back to the breath.

The sit, seven minutes
items.sub: Run the five steps every time you want out — you may run them several times in this sit.

blocks.prompt: The three words you said out loud when you named what came up. Then write what you were afraid would happen if you said them.

blocks.v: Twelve minutes on the timer
Read the line you wrote and closed the book on, back in week one. Read it once, out loud. Then settle first — do not skip the settling into the writing. It is the tether.

Silence surfaces things. That is not a side effect, it is the mechanism. If what surfaces today is grief, or old material arriving with your whole body attached to it, that is not a cut corner and this list will not close it. That belongs in a licensed room with a person trained for it, and needing that is normal — it is not a failure of the practice and it is not a failure of you.
blocks.title: Before you begin

items.head: Read the line
items.sub: From week one's journal. Out loud, once.

items.head: Settle first
items.sub: Slow-down three minutes, body scan five. Do not skip these into the writing.

items.head: Twelve minutes on the timer
items.sub: Feet on the floor. Let it be in the room with you. Not thinking about it — that is analysis, and analysis is how you have kept it at arm's length.

items.head: Run the five steps every time you want out
items.sub: You may run them nine times in twelve minutes. Nine is a good number.

items.head: Stop when the timer goes
items.sub: Even mid-sentence. Especially mid-sentence. Stopping on purpose is as much of the skill as staying.

items.head: Write, by hand
items.sub: One question only — what did it cost me to keep outrunning it. Hours, people, rooms you did not walk into.

items.head: Read it standing, out loud
items.sub: Then say it plainly to Him. I have been carrying this and I am putting it down in front of you. I am not picking it back up today.

items.head: Something ordinary with your hands
items.sub: Twenty minutes. Dishes, weeding, a walk. Not the phone. This is how a body comes back down.

blocks.text: Pour out your heart before Him. God is a refuge for us.
blocks.why: Pour out — not tidy up, not resolve, not present it well.

blocks.prompt: The thing I most don't want to be true is ___. Write it, then stay in the chair one more minute before you close the book.

blocks.v: This has to survive my worst week

You have had a room built for you for three weeks. Now you find out how it was made. Everyone can keep a floor for eleven days — the women still praying next spring are the ones who had a plan for the Wednesday they didn't.

items.head: Write the heading first
items.sub: This has to survive my worst week. Look at it the whole time you write the rest.

items.head: The daily floor
items.sub: What, how long, where, and a clock time. Then ask if you could do it on the worst day of last year. If no, halve it. If still no, halve it again.

items.head: The four-minute version
items.sub: Written separately, in one sentence. Extended exhales, the phrase eight times, one line to Him. Yours will be close to that.

items.head: The weekly beam
items.sub: One longer practice, with a named day and a named hour. If you cannot name the hour you do not have a beam, you have a wish.

items.head: The repair
items.sub: One sentence, written before you need it, including the clause — and I say nothing to anyone about the gap.

blocks.v: I have never once had a woman come back and tell me her floor was too small. Halve whatever you wrote — small is what survives.
blocks.title: On halving
Done means
items: The heading written first
The daily floor written and halved at least once
The four-minute version written as one sentence
The weekly beam named with a day and an hour
The repair sentence written, ending with the no-accounting clause
blocks.demo: Read your floor out loud. Could you do it on the worst day of last year — yes, without thinking about it?

blocks.prompt: The daily floor: what, how long, where, and a clock time. Could I do this on the worst day of last year? If you hesitated, halve it now. Then, the four-minute version, in one sentence.

blocks.v: The longest sit of the program
You are ready for it. All four shapes are in your body now, not just in your notes.

items.head: The word, said once

blocks.why: The wind, the earthquake, the fire, then the low whisper — spoken to a man who had just been fed and made to sleep. The body first, then the quiet, then the voice. This whole program is four thousand years old.

days.title: Read the Card Out Loud, Standing

blocks.v: Four weeks ago

Four weeks ago, five minutes was unbearable. Tonight, read your card out loud, standing, as far as you can get from memory. Floor, four-minute version, beam, repair. No preamble and no apology — if you catch yourself apologizing for it, read it again.

Brooke's spoken blessing for the end of this program — the words she says over a room on the last night — has not been recorded yet. Until it is, this closing day stands on the card itself and on what four weeks of sitting have actually built in you.
